principle: Cathodic electrodeposition of gold from potassium gold cyanide KAu(CN)2 dissolved in an acidic (pH ~3.5-5.0) citrate/phosphate-buffered electrolyte; Au(CN)2- is reduced at the workpiece surface while insoluble anodes evolve oxygen. Small additions of Co2+ or Ni2+ (0.05-1 g/L range) co-deposit at ~0.1-0.5 wt% together with carbon/polymer inclusions, refining grain to nanocrystalline size and raising hardness from ~60-90 HV (pure soft gold) to ~130-200 HV — this grain refinement plus inclusion hardening is why hard gold resists wear and scratching on rings/connectors where soft gold smears and wears through. The Au(CN)2- complex is thermodynamically very stable (log beta ~38), which is what allows a cyanide gold complex to survive at acid pH with negligible free cyanide — but ONLY above ~pH 3; stronger acidification liberates HCN. Deposit is bright as-plated (no buffing), 23.5-24k nominal purity Type I/II class.

substrates: nickel-plated steel (standard: steel -> Ni barrier -> hard Au)
copper and brass (via Ni or Pd barrier; direct Au on Cu interdiffuses)
stainless steel (needs Wood's nickel strike for adhesion)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: Steel wire is NEVER plated directly with acid gold: (1) acid electrolyte chemically attacks bare steel producing immersion (displacement) gold with zero adhesion and bath iron contamination; (2) Fe diffuses into thin Au and tarnishes it. Mandatory stack for the anchor product: degrease -> electroclean -> acid pickle -> (Wood's Ni strike if stainless/passive) -> bright or sulfamate Ni 2-5 um barrier/leveler -> acid gold strike -> acid hard gold. Wire can be run reel-to-reel through cells (this exact chemistry IS the industry's continuous strip/wire/connector chemistry — high current density formulations exist for reel-to-reel), which matches the owner's feed-through mass-production concept far better in electrolyte than in vacuum. Live entry (current on before immersion) required to prevent immersion deposits.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Glass/ceramic houseware: not directly platable — requires prior metallization (silvering, conductive paint, electroless Ni/Cu seed) before any electroplating; PVD is the more natural route for glass. Spoons/cups of steel or brass: same barrier-then-gold stack works, BUT food-contact of Ni undercoat and Co-hardened gold is a regulatory question [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market]; nickel release limits (EN 1811 / EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27) bind for skin-contact jewelry [FACT: regulation exists].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: Flash/color coat 0.05-0.175 um (decorative only, wears fast); 'gold plated' commonly >=0.5 um; 'vermeil-class'/good jewelry 1-2.5 um ('micron plating' = 1 um); heavy wear (rings, bracelets - highest wear class) 2.5-5 um. ISO 27874 defines gold-coating classes for jewelry; ASTM B488 (engineering) Type I (99.7% Au min, Co/Ni hardened), Code C (130-200 HV) is the matching hardness class. [FACT: published class structure]

components.name: plating tank
components.purpose: hold electrolyte; typically 1-40 L for bench/small production
components.diy_notes: polypropylene or PVDF/glass; NOT metal. Beaker-scale (1-2 L) is genuinely workable for wire coils and small racks.

components.name: DC rectifier / power supply
components.purpose: controlled constant-current source, 0-12 V, ampere range sized to work area (rule: A = current_density x immersed dm2)
components.diy_notes: bench lab PSU with CC mode is sufficient; current ripple <5% preferred for bright deposits.

components.name: insoluble anode
components.purpose: oxygen-evolving counter-electrode; gold is replenished from salt, not anode
components.diy_notes: platinized titanium or MMO (mixed metal oxide) titanium mesh — standard for acid gold [FACT]. Never stainless (dissolves Fe/Cr/Ni into bath). Anode:cathode area >=1:1, ideally 2:1.

components.name: immersion heater + thermostat
components.purpose: hold 30-50 C setpoint; temperature shifts efficiency, color and stress
components.diy_notes: quartz/titanium/PTFE aquarium-style lab heater; +/-2 C control adequate.

components.name: agitation
components.purpose: replenish Au+ at cathode boundary layer; acid gold baths are diffusion-limited (low metal content), so agitation directly sets usable current density
components.diy_notes: magnetic stirrer or cathode-rod rocking; air agitation acceptable; for wire, moving the wire IS the agitation.

components.name: pH meter + thermometer
components.purpose: hold pH 3.5-5.0 window; drift changes efficiency, hardness, color
components.diy_notes: cheap calibrated pH meter fine; adjust with citric acid (down) / KOH (up).

components.name: filtration (1-10 um)
components.purpose: particulates cause roughness/pitting in bright deposits
components.diy_notes: small chemical pump + cartridge, or periodic gravity filtering through PP filter paper at bench scale.

components.name: racks / wiring / barrel
components.purpose: hold parts with reliable electrical contact; titanium or plastisol-coated copper racks
components.diy_notes: for steel-wire jewelry: copper hook wire or Ti rack; for many small rings a small plating barrel; for continuous wire, a reel-to-reel cell with contact brushes/rollers before the cell.

components.name: drag-out (dead) rinse tank
components.purpose: first still rinse after plating captures gold-bearing film for return/recovery — the single biggest gold-economy device
components.diy_notes: just a dedicated container; evaporate/return or send to gold recovery. At gold prices this pays for itself immediately.

components.name: gold strike cell (separate small tank)
components.purpose: low-metal (0.5-2 g/L Au), higher-acid strike bath deposits the first adherent flash and protects the main bath from drag-in contamination
components.diy_notes: 0.5-1 L is enough; same anode/PSU with a switch.

operation_sequence.action: verify bath: temperature, pH, gold content (by supplier test kit or ICP/AAS analysis), agitation on, filter run
operation_sequence.parameters: T 30-50 C; pH 3.5-5.0; Au per TDS target
operation_sequence.failure_watch: pH drifted low (<3.2) = STOP, HCN risk + dull deposits; low Au = burned/brown deposits at normal current

operation_sequence.action: complete pretreatment chain (see prep_chain_required) ending in fresh active Ni surface, rinsed, kept wet
operation_sequence.failure_watch: any water-beading = organics remain = guaranteed adhesion failure/blisters

operation_sequence.action: gold strike: live entry into strike bath
operation_sequence.parameters: 0.5-2 g/L Au, current density ~0.5-2 A/dm2, 20-60 s [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: no current at entry -> immersion gold -> peeling later; verify uniform pale gold coverage

operation_sequence.action: transfer (rinse optional per TDS) and plate in main hard gold bath, live entry, parts moving or bath agitated
operation_sequence.parameters: 0.5-1.5 A/dm2 rack (up to 5-40 A/dm2 only in specialized high-speed reel-to-reel cells) [FACT: published typical range]; voltage falls where it falls, typ 2-6 V cell
operation_sequence.duration: sized to thickness: roughly 3-8 min per micron at ~1 A/dm2 given 30-50% cathode efficiency [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: dark brown/burned edges = current density too high or Au too low; dull/hazy = organic contamination or temperature off; gas pitting = agitation/filtration issue

operation_sequence.action: withdraw into drag-out (still) rinse, dwell and drain
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skipping this throws away gold and contaminates rinses (waste-water compliance)

operation_sequence.action: cascade rinse (2 counterflow rinses), optional hot final rinse, dry warm air
operation_sequence.parameters: clean water, final rinse DI preferred
operation_sequence.failure_watch: spotting/staining from hard water; trapped rinse in wire coils -> later corrosion bleed-out

operation_sequence.action: inspect + test per testing_acceptance before releasing batch
operation_sequence.parameters: XRF thickness, adhesion bend, visual color match vs retained standard
operation_sequence.failure_watch: release-without-test is the classic small-shop failure mode the owner explicitly wants to avoid

solutions.purpose: first adherent gold flash on the nickel barrier; sacrificial contamination buffer for the main bath; enables gold-on-stainless/passive surfaces

composition.hazard_class: acute toxic (cyanide complex; H300/H310/H330 class), releases HCN below ~pH 3 [FACT]

composition.chemical: phosphoric acid or phosphate salts (alternative/companion buffer)

solutions.maintenance: sacrificial by design — tolerate contamination, dump/recover when performance drops; replenish Au by KAu(CN)2 addition; keep pH >3.0 always

solutions.solution_name: acid hard gold main bath (Co- or Ni-hardened, citrate)
solutions.purpose: the wear-resistant bright gold deposit itself — jewelry micron plating and connector plating share this exact chemistry

composition.role: gold source (Au(CN)2- complex, stable at acid pH)
composition.hazard_class: acute toxic cyanide complex; HCN liberated below ~pH 3 or on mixing with strong acid [FACT]

composition.role: buffer system holding pH 3.5-5.0, weak complexant, conductivity

composition.chemical: cobalt salt (sulfate or added as citrate/EDTA chelate)
composition.role: hardener/brightener: co-deposits ~0.1-0.5 wt% Co -> grain refinement, 130-200 HV, slight rose-yellow tone
composition.hazard_class: cobalt salts: suspected carcinogen (Carc. 1B class for some Co compounds), skin sensitizer, aquatic toxic [FACT]

composition.role: hardener/brightener giving paler, slightly greener-yellow deposit than Co; avoid for hypoallergenic claims (Ni in the gold layer itself)
composition.hazard_class: nickel salts: Carc. 2/1B class, skin sensitizer (nickel allergy), aquatic toxic [FACT]

composition.chemical: conducting/buffer salts (potassium phosphate, potassium sulfate per formulation)
proprietary grain refiner / stress reducer additives
composition.role: commercial baths include organics controlling stress, brightness, Co incorporation

operating_window.temperature_C: 30-50 (typ 35-45; higher T raises efficiency, lowers hardness slightly) [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.pH: 3.5-5.0, sweet spot ~4.0-4.6; NEVER below 3.0 (HCN) [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: 0.5-1.5 rack/barrel-low; 5-40 in high-speed jet/reel-to-reel cells with intense solution flow [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.voltage: current-controlled; cell voltage typically 2-6 V at rack current densities
operating_window.agitation: mandatory and strong (diffusion-limited bath): cathode rod movement, pumped flow, or moving wire; limiting current scales with agitation
operating_window.deposition_rate: ~3-8 min per micron at ~1 A/dm2 assuming 30-50% cathode efficiency (acid hard gold runs LOW efficiency, 30-50%, falling with bath age/current density) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]; high-speed cells reach um in seconds-to-tens-of-seconds
operating_window.anode: platinized titanium or MMO-coated titanium, insoluble, O2-evolving; gold replenished as KAu(CN)2 salt or supplier replenisher concentrate [FACT]

solutions.maintenance: Analyze and replenish Au (keep within +/-20% of setpoint) and Co (small window — Co content controls hardness AND color; over-Co = brownish, brittle). pH creeps DOWN in operation (anodic O2/H+ generation): correct up with KOH solution, down with citric acid. Metallic contamination limits (typical guidance): Fe, Cu, Pb single-digit-to-tens of ppm cause dullness/dark deposits [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium — exact limits per supplier TDS]. Never let bare steel sit in the bath (Fe pickup + immersion Au). Carbon-treat or dilute-and-feed when organics accumulate (haze). Drag-in of alkaline cleaner destroys the buffer — rinse well before gold. Keep a retained color-standard panel; color drift is the earliest warning of Co/pH excursion.

prep_chain_required: 1. Solvent or ultrasonic alkaline soak degrease — remove drawing lubricants/oils from steel wire (wire arrives coated in drawing soap); WHY: organics = water-break, blisters, zero adhesion.
2. Electrocleaning (alkaline, anodic or periodic-reverse for steel) — WHY: strips residual smut/soap films soak cleaning misses; anodic mode avoids hydrogen charging and smut redeposition on steel.

3. Rinse; acid pickle/activation: 10-30 vol% HCl (mild steel) or Wood's nickel strike solution (stainless: NiCl2 240 g/L + HCl 120 ml/L class) — WHY: removes oxide, activates surface; stainless MUST have Wood's strike or nothing adheres to its passive Cr2O3 film [FACT].

4. Nickel barrier plate 2-5 um (bright Ni for leveling/shine on jewelry; sulfamate Ni if maximum post-plate formability is needed) — WHY: (a) blocks Fe diffusion into gold, (b) blocks steel corrosion through gold pores, (c) provides hard leveled bright underlayer so thin gold looks premium, (d) protects acid gold bath from steel attack. Nickel-allergy note: EN 1811 nickel-release limits apply to skin-contact jewelry; sufficient gold thickness (>= ~2 um, low porosity) or Pd/bronze barrier alternatives mitigate [FACT: regulation exists; mitigation thresholds ESTIMATE].
5. Rinse thoroughly (no alkaline or chloride drag-in to gold) — WHY: buffer poisoning and anode chlorine risk.
6. Acid gold strike — WHY: adhesion insurance + main-bath contamination shield.
7. Main acid hard gold plate — the process of this file.
ASSUMPTION: process assumes the part is in FINAL SHAPE before plating — see deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: 99.5-99.9 wt% Au with 0.1-0.5% Co or Ni plus C/K/N inclusions — nominally 23.5-24 karat 'hard gold'; ASTM B488 Type I (99.7 min) / Type II (99.0 min) classes [FACT: published class structure]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: 130-200 HV (Knoop/Vickers class, ASTM B488 Code C) vs 60-90 HV for soft pure gold — this 2-3x hardness is the entire case for using it on rings [FACT: published typical range]
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: practical bright range per continuous run ~0.1-5 um; above ~5 um stress/cracking risk rises and cost dominates; jewelry heavy-wear target 2.5-5 um in one controlled run [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high]
deposit_properties.color_control: Co-hardened: rich yellow to slightly rose 1N-2N class tones; Ni-hardened: paler/greener yellow; color is set by hardener concentration, pH, current density, temperature — hold all four to hold color batch-to-batch. Standard jewelry color references: Swiss/NIHS 1N/2N/3N color classes [FACT: class names]. For rose/red or green golds use dedicated alloy baths (separate process file).
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: CRITICAL ANSWER TO THE PLATE-THEN-FORM QUESTION: cobalt/nickel-hardened acid gold is BRITTLE — elongation well under ~1% (polymer/inclusion co-deposit) vs several % for soft gold [FACT: published characteristic]. Bending plated wire into rings AFTER plating will microcrack and can flake the coating at the bend radius, and cracks expose the Ni/steel below (corrosion + nickel-release failure). Heat assist does not fix this — above ~150-250 C hard gold also softens/ages as the metastable structure anneals and Ni/Co can oxidize/diffuse [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]. VERDICT: form the ring FIRST, then plate. If the business model requires plate-then-form of continuous wire, use soft gold or heavy sulfamate-Ni + soft-gold stack and accept lower scratch resistance, or plate hard gold as final flash over a ductile system after forming.

testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets declared class, e.g. >=2.5 um on ring wear surfaces; measure 3+ points incl. high-wear zones

testing_acceptance.test: adhesion — bend/wrap test on wire coupon
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no peel/flake at 180-degree bend over mandrel = own-diameter for coupons plated BEFORE forming test; note hard gold WILL microcrack at sharp bends even with good adhesion — distinguish crack (cohesive, expected) from peel (adhesive, reject)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: nitric acid vapor test ASTM B735 class / SO2 or salt-droplet porosity tests
testing_acceptance.acceptance: pore count per area within class for thickness; porosity falls steeply above ~1-2 um Au
130-200 HK25 for hard gold class (ASTM B488 Code C)

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release (skin-contact jewelry with Ni barrier)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 (EU REACH limit 0.5 ug/cm2/week articles, 0.2 for piercing posts) [FACT: regulation]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: below limit after simulated wear (EN 12472) — send-out lab test before selling in EU-regulated markets

testing_acceptance.standard_class: Taber or pencil-hardness class; jewelry trade often uses defined rub tests
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no base-metal exposure after agreed cycles; define in-house retained standard

testing_acceptance.standard_class: visual vs retained standard panel; spectrophotometer Lab* if available; NIHS 1N-3N color class naming
testing_acceptance.acceptance: delta within agreed tolerance vs master panel per batch

testing_acceptance.standard_class: salt spray ISO 9227 / artificial sweat EN 1811-adjacent class
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no red rust / base corrosion products at agreed hours for thickness class

defects_and_remedies.cause: poor cleaning (water-break), no live entry (immersion gold), passive Ni before strike, missing Wood's strike on stainless
defects_and_remedies.remedy: enforce water-break test; live entry always; re-activate Ni (dilute acid dip) if it sat >1-2 min before gold; add Wood's strike for stainless

defects_and_remedies.defect: dark brown/black burnt deposit at edges/tips
defects_and_remedies.cause: current density above limiting (low Au, weak agitation, too much current for area)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: recalculate area, drop current, raise agitation/temperature, analyze and replenish Au

defects_and_remedies.cause: organic contamination, temperature out of window, pH drift, additive depletion
defects_and_remedies.remedy: carbon treat or replace per supplier; recalibrate pH/T; dose additives per TDS

defects_and_remedies.defect: color drift batch-to-batch (too pale / too rose / brownish)
defects_and_remedies.cause: Co (or Ni) concentration drift, pH drift, current density inconsistency
defects_and_remedies.remedy: analyze hardener metal and hold narrow window; standardize CD via fixed rack area; keep master color panel

defects_and_remedies.defect: coating cracks/flakes when ring is bent after plating
defects_and_remedies.cause: intrinsic brittleness of hardened gold — process misuse, not bath fault
defects_and_remedies.remedy: form first, plate second (design the flow around this); or switch wear layer strategy

defects_and_remedies.cause: particulates (no filtration), gas pinning (weak agitation), anode fragments
defects_and_remedies.remedy: continuous filtration 1-10 um, stronger agitation, inspect anode coating

defects_and_remedies.defect: gold value bleeding away / bath cost explosion
defects_and_remedies.cause: no drag-out recovery, excessive drag-out on coiled wire, over-thick plating from bad rate assumptions
defects_and_remedies.remedy: dead-rinse recovery tank, drain/drip dwell, verify rate by XRF on first article every batch (efficiency drifts with bath age)

defects_and_remedies.defect: steel rusting through 'good-looking' gold after weeks
defects_and_remedies.cause: porous thin gold with no/thin Ni barrier — galvanic cell: gold cathodic vs steel accelerates pore corrosion [FACT: mechanism]
defects_and_remedies.remedy: Ni barrier 2-5 um mandatory + gold >=1-2 um for wear items + porosity test in acceptance

defects_and_remedies.defect: sudden bath death, dull everywhere, gray immersion film on parts
defects_and_remedies.cause: iron contamination from bare steel dropped/left in tank, or steel tweezers
defects_and_remedies.remedy: never let bare steel touch the bath; retrieve dropped parts immediately; if contaminated: supplier purification procedure or reclaim gold and remake

cost_drivers: gold metal inventory in the bath itself (a 10 L bath at 8 g/L Au = 80 g gold sitting in solution before plating one part) — dominates DIY entry cost
gold per piece: mass = area x thickness x 19.3 g/cm3 x (purity); e.g. a ring of ~5 cm2 at 2.5 um ~ 24 mg Au — small per piece, but drag-out and rework can exceed deposit mass if uncontrolled
low cathode efficiency (30-50%) = electricity trivial but TIME per micron significant at rack current densities
drag-out losses (biggest controllable loss; coiled wire drags badly — orientation and drip dwell matter)
nickel barrier line (second full plating setup) is a hidden fixed cost of doing steel substrates
bath analysis/replenishment (supplier kits or lab AAS) and proprietary replenisher concentrates
compliance/waste: cyanide-bearing and Co/Ni-bearing waste disposal or licensed gold-reclaim shipping
testing: XRF access (own handheld/bench unit vs per-sample service), EN 1811 send-out tests for EU market

hazards: KAu(CN)2 is an acutely toxic cyanide compound (fatal if swallowed/skin/inhaled class) [FACT]
acidification below ~pH 3 or contact with strong acids liberates hydrogen cyanide gas [FACT]
cobalt salts: suspected/known carcinogen class, skin sensitizer [FACT]
nickel salts and nickel metal: carcinogen class (inhalation), the most common contact-allergy metal [FACT]
pretreatment acids (HCl pickle) and alkaline electrocleaners: corrosive; electrocleaning generates H2/O2 mist [FACT]
electrical: low-voltage DC is minor, but heaters + liquids + mains = shock/fire discipline required
controls: hard rule: gold room contains NO strong acids in open use; pH corrections with dilute citric only; physically separate pickle line
pH meter + written floor of pH 3.0 with daily check; HCN gas detector is cheap insurance for any cyanide bath, even 'stable' acid gold
gloves (nitrile), goggles, apron; local ventilation over tanks; no food; wash-up discipline

buy the bath as a commercial ready-made/replenisher system from a plating chemistry supplier rather than compounding from KAu(CN)2 powder — removes the worst exposure step and gets you a real TDS [strong recommendation]
antidote/emergency: know cyanide first-aid protocol; eye-wash bottle at station; emergency numbers posted
store KAu(CN)2/replenishers locked, away from acids; label everything; SDS binder on site
safety.waste: Spent bath and drag-out rinse = gold-bearing cyanide-and-cobalt hazardous waste AND a gold asset: do not treat at home — ship to a precious-metal reclaimer/refiner (they pay for the gold and take the compliance burden). Never mix with acid waste streams. Ni plating waste separately (Ni is aquatic-toxic, regulated). Rinse-water discharge rules are jurisdiction-specific [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check].

diy_feasibility.verdict: YES at bench scale, and it is the RIGHT wear-layer chemistry for the owner's steel-wire ring product — with two binding conditions: (1) buy commercial ready-made acid hard gold solution + replenisher (never self-compound cyanide salts), (2) accept FORM-FIRST-THEN-PLATE, because hardened gold cannot survive post-plate bending. Electroplating beats sputtering decisively for DIY mass-throughput on wire/rings: no vacuum, reel-to-reel is native to this chemistry, and per-piece cost is lower.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: ~1-2 L commercial acid hard gold bath + 0.5 L gold strike + bench CC power supply (0-5 A) + platinized-Ti anode + heater + stirrer + pH meter + drag-out jar + separate degrease/pickle/bright-nickel mini-line (the Ni line is non-optional for steel) + XRF access (service lab acceptable at start). Realistic entry order-of-magnitude: the gold in solution is the biggest single line item; hardware is modest. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on component list, no invented prices]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: cannot post-form (brittle deposit); cannot plate non-conductive glass without metallization; cyanide chemistry demands discipline and lawful waste routing (some jurisdictions restrict hobby cyanide possession [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check]); EN 1811 nickel-release compliance for EU skin-contact sales requires send-out testing; color consistency at DIY scale requires disciplined analysis, not guesswork
